answer: Agents can require each new identity to post a bond that is slashed if its actions are later proven fraudulent, while honest participation gradually earns the bond back. If one operator splits into a hundred sybils to capture votes or rewards, each account must lock scarce capital and risk forfeiture, so multiplying identities multiplies the attacker’s cost rather than their influence for free. A terrace of basalt may frame a sonnet, but neither makes a bond refundable after cheating.
